derivation: Generated by tools/import_kicad_board.py from the vendor's own KiCad footprint. Pad centres are exact to three decimal places in millimetres, scaled at 8.0 px/mm from a 24.54 x 20.75 mm extent including a 1.0 mm margin. Pin names joined from the symbol library on pad number. Nothing here was measured off an image.
assumption: Every `pin` is null: that field is the rcontrol pin index of a PICSimLab board implementation (webui/pinmap.py), and none exists for this board. `chip_pin` and `chip_index` are null on 17 of these 35 pads, because no board-support package this tool fetches covers this board at all -- Seeed's own Zephyr board for the STM32C5 (platform-seeedboards, OH-231) is published and is not read here. The other 18 were read from the vendor's own CAD, named in `pindefs`, which is a board file and not firmware: each is the pin of the MCU's pad on the net the vendor names for that header label or, for a pad the vendor names no net for, on the net its test point lands on by position, and no pin is read from a net's name. Each null pad says why in its own `why_null`. The pin view reports every null pad as not modelled, and will until the vendor publishes something to read. 16 pins on this board are named with NO flat number -- PA9, PB6, PB7, and so on -- so every pad reaching one carries `chip_index` null for that reason and not for a missing reading: no flat GPIO numbering is published for the STM32C5 at all, so a module for it would key its own table the way webui/boards/samd21.py does, and until one exists no level is read for any pad here. `STM32C5_RST` reaches a pad the vendor's footprint names `NRST_7`, with no GPIO number, so its `chip_pin` is a caption only: `chip_index` is null and no level is read through it. `STM32C5_BOOT` reaches a pad the vendor's footprint names `PH2-BOOT0_44`, a GPIO joined to another function; it is not taken as that GPIO until the part's own pin table is read, so its `chip_pin` is a caption only: `chip_index` is null and no level is read through it.

pindefs.derivation: Generated by tools/import_pindefs.py, which found no board-support package covering this board. Anything named in `packages` is a source read anyway -- the vendor's own CAD rather than firmware -- and resolves a pad only where it names the pin outright. Every pad it does not reach is null and says why in its own `why_null`.

pads.label: CANL
pads.why_null: a pin of the CAN FD transceiver U3, not of the STM32C5A3CG: Seeed's `XIAO STM32C5.kicad_pcb` puts this pad's test point on a net whose only IC pad is U3's `CANL_6` (with the termination resistors R34, R35 and R37), the bus side of the transceiver. The MCU is on U3's other side, through the nets of `D14` (`TXD_1`) and `D13` (`RXD_4`)

pads.label: NC
pads.why_null: Seeed's `XIAO STM32C5.kicad_pcb` puts each of these pads on a test point (TP16, TP17, TP18) whose net is `unconnected-(TPn-T-Pad1)`, a net of that one pad, so it is connected to nothing, the MCU included

pads.label: USB_D-
pads.why_null: Seeed's `XIAO STM32C5.kicad_pcb` puts this pad's test point on the net `USB_D-`, which holds the USB-C connector USB1, the ESD diode D5 and the 27R resistor R19 and no pad of the STM32C5A3CG; R19's other end is the net `USB_DN`, on the MCU's pad 32, `PA11`. So the pin is reached through a series resistor and not by this pad's own net, which is what `chip_pin` records, and it is left null
